mainEntity.name: What's the maximum fence height allowed in Troy, Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Residential fences in Troy cannot exceed 6 feet in height. This includes the posts and any decorative elements. Fences shorter than 4 feet typically don't require a building permit, but any fence 4 feet or taller requires review by the Planning Department. Commercial properties may have different height allowances.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to build a fence in Troy?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your fence is under 4 feet tall, a building permit is generally not required. However, if your fence is between 4 and 6 feet tall — which most privacy fences are — you need a Planning Department review. Submit a site plan showing the fence location relative to your property lines. We handle all permit applications for our customers.

mainEntity.name: What's the best wood for a privacy fence in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Western Red Cedar is the best choice for most Michigan homeowners. It's naturally rot-resistant, stable in Michigan's humidity, and develops a beautiful patina over time. Pressure-treated pine is a good budget alternative, but it's heavier, more prone to checking and twisting, and requires more maintenance. Cedar will typically outlast pressure-treated pine by 5-10 years in Michigan conditions.

mainEntity.name: How much does a cedar privacy fence cost in Troy, Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: A custom cedar privacy fence installed by a professional contractor typically runs $25-35 per linear foot in the Troy area. For an average Troy lot, expect a total installed cost of $5,000 to $10,000 depending on design complexity, number of gates, and site conditions.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to install a custom wood fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most standard residential installations take 4 to 6 working days. The timeline depends on lot size, soil conditions, weather, and design complexity. Board-on-board designs take slightly longer than standard shadowbox or dog-ear fences because of the overlapping picket pattern.

mainEntity.name: Does a wood privacy fence increase home value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — multiple studies show that a quality wood privacy fence adds value to a home, with an estimated 50-70% return on investment at resale. In Troy's competitive real estate market, a well-maintained privacy fence is a significant selling point that adds usable square footage to the home.

Board-on-board is a fence design where pickets are installed on both sides of the stringers, with each picket overlapping the next by about an inch. This creates a solid visual barrier with no gaps — unlike shadowbox fencing, which has alternating gaps. Board-on-board looks the same from both sides and provides maximum privacy.

mainEntity.name: How deep do fence posts need to be in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fence posts in Michigan need to be set at least 36 inches deep, and we recommend 42 inches for gate posts and corner posts. Michigan's frost line reaches 36-42 inches in most of Oakland County. Setting posts below the frost line prevents frost heave during spring freeze-thaw cycles, which is the most common cause of premature fence failure.
